_note: The five paid flowers, generated with create_image_pixflux against the forced palettes in palettes.json (built by scripts/flowers/palettes.py). Every palette keeps the sunflower's own greens and stem brown and changes only the petal ramp, which is what makes six species read as one garden. Canvases match the sunflower stage each sprite stands in for (bloom 172x244, bud 136x220, sprout 108x76, all rounded to the pixel grid's multiple of 4), so at the same display height they carry the same apparent pixel size. Re-running with the same seed + palette reproduces these. The sunflower itself is older hand-kept art and has no job here.

daisy-bloom@seed11.why: Head about a fifth of the canvas, so at the 92px it ships at the flower read as a white dot on a stick. The fix was in the prompt, not the seed: asking for the head to fill the top half of the image.

lily-bloom@seed11.why: Same problem as the daisy, worse — a lily's petals are thin, so a small head lost them entirely at display size.

daisy-bloom@palette.why: The white-petalled flowers cannot use a forced palette. A palette makes the generator return the art flattened onto its lightest colour instead of transparency, and on the daisy and the lily that lightest colour IS the petal — so keying the backdrop took the petals with it and left a yellow disc floating on a stem. Both are generated palette-free instead, with the greens named in the prompt; the backdrop then comes back a pale green the petals never use, and keys cleanly.

lily-bloom@palette.why: Same as the daisy: cream petals the same colour as the forced backdrop, so keying ate holes through them.

lily-bloom@white.why: A white lily on light-green grass is nearly all highlight: at 92px its petals lost their edges and the whole flower read as a pale smudge, with a broken orange outline. Every other species carries a colour that holds at display size, so the lily became a pink stargazer — still the most-planted lily there is, and it survives the downscale.

rose-sprout@wide.why: An attempt to widen the seedling to the sunflower sprout's chunkier proportions, by asking for big leaves spreading left and right. It drew the leaves genuinely detached — floating either side of a stemless mound of soil — and the clean-up then binned them as strays. The narrower first batch is kept: it is a little slighter than the sunflower's seedling, but it is a plant.

rose-bud@seed11.why: Drew one leaf detached from a hair-thin stem; the clean-up binned the leaf as a stray and what shipped was a bud on a bare wire. Re-prompted for a thick stem and a leaf either side.

lily-bud@cream.why: Cream tips, drawn against the white lily this species used to be. Once the bloom became a pink stargazer the bud had to follow, or a garden changed colour as it grew.
